title: Inverse image of an injective abelian sheaf is acyclic for site-object sections
statement: Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be small sites in the common universe [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention], and let $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be continuous and cocontinuous [def-weil-pbc-special-cocontinuous-functor](1). Let $g:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)$ be the geometric morphism associated to $u$ [def-trf-geometric-morphism]. If $I$ is an injective object of $\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal D)$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions], then for every $U\in\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal C)$ and every integer $p>0$ one has $$H^p(U,g^{-1}I)=0,$$ where $H^p(U,-)=R^p\Gamma(U,-)$ is the ordinary right derived functor of evaluation on abelian sheaves [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology].

source.place: Tag 0D6X, lemma-pullback-injective-pre-limp, specialized to the integer ring sheaf, whose module category is abelian sheaves.

proof.text: Put $F=g^{-1}I$. The continuous-cocontinuous adjunction theorem [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-cocontinuous-topos-adjunction] identifies the underlying set sheaf of $F$ with $V\mapsto I(u(V))$, including restriction maps. This identification also respects the abelian group operations: apply the same inverse-image functor to the addition, zero and negation maps of $I$; its finite-product comparison identifies addition with the componentwise addition on $I(u(V))$. Thus $F(V)=I(u(V))$ as abelian groups, naturally in $V$.

source.place: Tag 0D6X, lemma-pullback-injective-pre-limp, proof: the formula $g^{-1}=u^p$, using Sites Tag 00XR (lemma-when-shriek).

proof.text: Fix any covering $\mathcal U=\{U_t\to U\}_{t\in T}$ of $\mathcal C$. By continuity [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](3), $u(\mathcal U)=\{u(U_t)\to u(U)\}_{t\in T}$ is a covering of $\mathcal D$. For a tuple $\mathbf t=(t_0,\ldots,t_n)$ write $W_{\mathbf t}=U_{t_0}\times_U\cdots\times_U U_{t_n}$ and $P_{\mathbf t}=u(U_{t_0})\times_{u(U)}\cdots\times_{u(U)}u(U_{t_n})$, with the choices of [def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex]. The canonical comparison $c_{\mathbf t}:u(W_{\mathbf t})\to P_{\mathbf t}$ is invertible by induction on $n$: for $n=0$ it is the identity (up to the chosen product isomorphism); to append $t_n$, apply continuity (3)(b) to the original covering and the map $W_{(t_0,\ldots,t_{n-1})}\to U$, then use the preceding comparison. For each projection $\delta_j$ omitting one factor, $c_{\mathbf t\setminus t_j}\,u(\delta_j)=\delta_j\,c_{\mathbf t}$, because both sides have the same projections to every remaining factor and the product universal property makes such a map unique.

source.place: Tag 0D6X, proof: continuity sends a covering and all its iterated fibre products to the corresponding covering nerve; Sites Tag 00WV (definition-continuous).

proof.text: In degree $n\ge0$, step 1 identifies $\check{\mathcal C}^n(\mathcal U,F)$ with $\prod_{\mathbf t\in T^{n+1}}I(u(W_{\mathbf t}))$. Applying $I(c_{\mathbf t}^{-1})$ componentwise gives an isomorphism to $\prod_{\mathbf t\in T^{n+1}}I(P_{\mathbf t})=\check{\mathcal C}^n(u(\mathcal U),I)$. These are the groups and restriction differentials of [def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex]. The projection identity of step 2, contravariance of $I$, and the restriction formula of step 1 show that each omitting-factor restriction commutes with these isomorphisms. Hence their alternating sums commute too, so we obtain an isomorphism of Cech complexes (both are zero in negative degrees). Its inverse induces inverse maps on kernels modulo images. Consequently $\check H^p(\mathcal U,F)\cong\check H^p(u(\mathcal U),I)$. Since $I$ is an injective abelian sheaf on $\mathcal D$ and $u(\mathcal U)$ is a covering, [lem-weil-pbc-site-injective-cech-acyclic] makes the right side zero for every $p>0$. The common universe contains both small sites, their covering indices and the abelian-group values, as required by that lemma.

source.place: Tag 0D6X, proof: equality of Cech cohomology under the nerve identification; its cited module-injective vanishing Tag 03FC specializes here to abelian-injective vanishing Tag 03AW (lemma-injective-trivial-cech).

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-cech-vanishing-criterion] on $\mathcal C$ with $\mathcal B=\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal C)$, $\mathrm{Cov}$ the site's entire set of coverings, and the abelian sheaf $F$. All covering objects and all their iterated fibre products belong to $\mathcal B$. The coverings in $\mathrm{Cov}$ are cofinal, since any covering refines itself using the identity map on its index set and on each member. The required positive Cech vanishing for every covering is step 3. The criterion therefore gives $H^p(U,F)=0$ for every object $U$ and every $p>0$, with $H^p$ the ordinary right derived functor of evaluation specified in its statement. Substituting $F=g^{-1}I$ proves the assertion.

source.place: Tag 0D6X, first proof sentence, applying Tag 03F9 (lemma-cech-vanish-collection) with all objects and all coverings.
